title.en: Define marketing and distinguish it from selling

say.en: Old-fashioned firms made a product and then tried to sell it. Modern firms first find out what customers want. That shift is the marketing concept. In this lesson: Define marketing and distinguish it from selling.
Explain the marketing management philosophies.
Describe the functions of marketing.

body.en: Marketing is a social process by which individuals and groups obtain what they need and want through creating and exchanging products and value with others. Marketing management *philosophies* have evolved: the production concept (make products cheap and available), the product concept (make high-quality products), the selling concept (aggressive selling and promotion), the marketing concept (identify customer needs and satisfy them better than competitors) and the societal marketing concept (satisfy customers while protecting the long-term welfare of society and the environment).

points.en: Exchange to satisfy needs and wants

body.en: The *marketing mix* is the set of controllable variables a firm combines to satisfy its target market: the 4 Ps. Product (what is offered: features, quality, brand, packaging, label), Price (what customers pay: list price, discounts, credit terms), Place (how the product reaches customers: channels of distribution and physical distribution) and Promotion (how customers are informed and persuaded: advertising, personal selling, sales promotion and public relations). The four are interdependent and must fit together.

points.en: Promotion: advertising, selling, sales promotion, PR

problem.en: Distinguish marketing from selling on four points.

steps.en: Scope: selling is one part of marketing; marketing is wider.
Starting point: selling starts with the product; marketing starts with customer needs.
Focus: selling on the seller's needs; marketing on customer satisfaction.
End point: selling ends with the sale; marketing continues after it.

answer.en: Marketing is wider, customer-focused and continuous; selling is product-focused and ends at the sale.
